key_insight: RM-VLM combines language-generated reward machines with visual proposition grounding to guide reinforcement learning on tasks that depend on event history.
engineering_relevance: The approach reduces the need to hand-engineer environment-specific proposition labellers for visually observed, multi-step tasks.
method: An LLM converts a natural-language task description into a reward machine encoding temporal structure.
A VLM grounds the machine’s propositions in image observations during policy learning.
A VLM-based value estimator assesses progress toward reward-machine transitions to provide dense rewards.
evidence_signal: Across non-Markovian grid-world navigation, robotic manipulation, and 3D object collection, the abstract reports higher task success rates than existing VLM-based reward methods, without numerical results.
watch_item: Incorrect language-generated task logic or visual proposition grounding could produce misleading rewards and requires validation.
paper_title: RM-VLM: From Natural-Language Task Descriptions to Vision-Grounded Reward Machines
